params.body:
Phase 2 of `docs/design/sources-before-more-sources.md`, second platform. No cost,
no account, no decision needed: this one was ours.

## Silent since 12 March, and nothing ever broke

The feed answered 200 with ten items per country the whole time. But Google puts
**the same `<link>` in every item**, the address of the feed itself, and this
adapter used the link as the signal's url. The url is the dedup key. So the first
item ever seen for a country claimed it, and every trend after was "already
known". Six signals in total, one per country, all from the first day.

A healthy feed and a collector that threw all of it away, with no error and no
empty answer to notice. `adapter_runs` had it as `unknown` every round, which is
exactly the outcome that says "this adapter does not tell us what it fetched".

## The fix

- **The key is built from what makes a trend this trend**: the term and the
  country. A feed may not be trusted to hand out identities. Case and stray
  spaces do not make a new trend.
- **The `ht:` fields were never parsed**, because rss-parser drops what it is not
  told about. Traffic, picture and the news items under a term are read now.
  "brigitte macron" alone says nothing; the headline under it is what lets the
  classifier tell a youth signal from the weather.
- It reports what it fetched, so its outcome stops reading `unknown`.

This is also **the one platform source that still speaks for Belgium and the
Netherlands**: TikTok stopped publishing trends for both.

The test uses the feed as Google gave it on 20 September and asserts the bug in
one line: both items carry the same link, and must get two keys.

788 tests pass, 5 new.
params.title: Google Trends: a feed may not hand out identities
